name: Earnur

name: Aragorn II Elessar (King)

Chose to lay down his life at the end (in the manner of the ancient Numenorean kings) rather than decline into dotage.
source: LOTR Appendix A/B, 'Gondor and the Heirs of Anarion'

name: Pelendur

Predates the Ruling Stewards; not one of the 26 counted in that line. His accession year (c.1940) is the single least-certain date in this whole dataset -- only his death (1998) and the 1944 crisis are well corroborated; no birth year is attested anywhere found.

source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Gram
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Helm Hammerhand
notes: Both his sons killed by Dunlendings in the Long Winter siege of the Hornburg; Helm himself froze to death. Last king of the First Line.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Frealaf Hildeson
notes: Helm's sister-son; first king of the Second Line. Gave Isengard to Saruman.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Brytta Leofa
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Walda
notes: Killed by orcs near Dunharrow.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Folca the Hunter
notes: Died of a wound from the great boar of Everholt after clearing Rohan of its last orcs.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Folcwine
notes: His twin sons Folcred and Fastred died fighting for Gondor.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Fengel
notes: Unpopular; his son Thengel left for Gondor rather than stay.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Thengel
notes: Lived in Gondor and married Morwen of Lossarnach before returning to rule.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Theoden
notes: Last king of the Second Line. Killed at the Battle of the Pelennor Fields; avenged by his niece Eowyn.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'

name: Eomer Eadig
notes: Theoden's sister-son; first king of the Third Line.
source: LOTR Appendix A, 'The House of Eorl'
